The delegation, which arrived at the forward operating bases on Thursday, was led by the Commander of the Somali Land Forces, Major General Sahal Abdullahi Omar (Khaalid), accompanied by the Chairman of the First Degree Court of the Armed Forces, Colonel Hassan Ali Nuur Shuute, and other senior officers. The commanders visited the Leego and Jameeco areas of Buurhakaba district, where a fierce battle had taken place a day earlier between government forces and Al-Shabaab, resulting in significant casualties on both sides, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the battle . Acknowledging Losses, Claiming Victory General Khaalid met with field commanders and troops, receiving briefings on the latest security situation and the ongoing operations in the area. Addressing the soldiers, he acknowledged that both sides had suffered casualties in the recent fighting and offered condolences to the families of the fallen, while wishing a speedy recovery to the wounded. The General confirmed that at least 70 Al-Shabaab fighters were killed and more than that number wounded. His statement slightly revised the Defence Ministry’s earlier claim of 75 killed and 56 wounded, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the ministry’s statement . “The Somali National Army is not defeated in battle, and we want the Somali people to stand with us,” General Khaalid said. He added: “If you are real men, we do not fear death. We are ready and moving forward until we remove you from the country.” Fighting on Two Fronts The deployment of senior commanders to the frontlines reflects the government’s determination to press its advantage in the Bay region, where it is fighting not only Al-Shabaab but also forces aligned with Laftagareen. The political dispute with the former regional leader has created a second front in South West State, complicating the counterterrorism campaign and diverting resources. As reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the regional tensions , the fighting between federal forces and Laftagareen-aligned militias has escalated in recent weeks, with reports of heavy weapons and aerial strikes. The government has accused Laftagareen of coordinating with Al-Shabaab, allegations he denies. The commanders’ visit also included the Chairman of the First Degree Court of the Armed Forces, signaling that the government is preparing to process captured fighters and address legal accountability alongside military operations. The Kenyan Dimension The crisis is now spilling across the border. According to a report by The Standard, senior officials in Mogadishu have accused Kenya of harboring Somali terrorists and allowing them to plot violence against Somalia while allegedly taking refuge in Nairobi hotels under state protection. Speaker of the House of the People Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur has said the Federal Government of Somalia should demand answers from Kenya regarding the ongoing violence. His intervention places the parliament’s weight behind the accusation, elevating it from a security complaint to a formal political demand. The accusation lands on a relationship that has been carefully rebuilt over the past two years. In March 2026, Somali Ambassador to Kenya Jabril Ibrahim Abdulle held extensive talks with Kenyan Foreign Affairs Principal Secretary Korir Sing’Oei in Nairobi, focused on advancing the Joint Commission of Cooperation and finalizing pending MoUs in the Blue Economy, trade, and cross-border movement, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the diplomatic talks . Security cooperation has been a central pillar of that rebuilding. In April 2026, Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre met with Kenya’s Ambassador to Somalia, Cyprian Kubai Iringo, to discuss strengthening coordination on border security and regional stability, with both sides reaffirming their commitment to joint efforts against extremism, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the security talks . Kenya is also a troop-contributing country to AUSSOM, with 1,410 personnel deployed in Somalia, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the AU mission . The economic stakes are equally significant. Somalia is a major market for Kenyan miraa exports, a trade that supports tens of thousands of farmers and generates billions of shillings in foreign exchange. Kenya has formed a national committee to stabilize miraa prices and boost exports to Somalia, and the two countries have negotiated agreements to expand quotas, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the miraa trade and the planned miraa agreement . The miraa trade is sensitive to political disruption. In January 2025, female khat sellers in Mogadishu blocked the KM4 road in protest against increased taxes on Kenyan miraa, after the government restricted imports to a select few traders, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the protests . The episode illustrated how quickly trade measures can trigger public unrest and strain bilateral relations. The border itself has been a flashpoint. The reopening of key crossings in 2026 was a significant step toward normalizing trade and movement, as reported in FTL Somalia’s coverage of the border reopening. Any escalation of the current political dispute could put that progress at risk. Critical Note The deployment of General Khaalid and his senior officers to the frontlines is a significant escalation in the government’s military campaign. It signals that the federal leadership is treating the South West State as a priority and is willing to commit its most senior commanders to the fight. The General’s remarks, mixing condolences with a defiant vow to continue the offensive, reflect the dual nature of the mission: acknowledging the cost of the battle while projecting resolve. But the casualty figures remain contested. The Defence Ministry claimed 75 Al-Shabaab fighters killed. General Khaalid said 70. Soldiers who spoke to Reuters after the battle described far heavier losses on the government side. The government has not provided a detailed account of its own casualties, and the discrepancy between its claims and the accounts of its soldiers is a gap that transparency would help close. The Kenyan dimension adds another layer of complexity. The accusation that Nairobi is harboring terrorists is a serious charge, and it comes at a time when relations between the two countries are already strained. The miraa trade is a vital economic link, and any disruption to it would harm both countries. But the Speaker’s demand for answers from Kenya is a reminder that security cooperation between Mogadishu and Nairobi has limits, and that the political crisis in South West State is not confined to Somalia’s borders. The presence of the military court chairman at the frontlines is a reminder that this is not only a military operation. It is also a legal and political one. The government is fighting Al-Shabaab, but it is also fighting Laftagareen, and the two conflicts are entangled. Whether the commanders can translate their visit into a decisive military advantage will depend not only on their tactics but on whether the political dispute with Laftagareen is resolved, and whether the regional tensions with Kenya can be contained. الرابعة إلى جانب أندية بيراميدز المصري، وحوريا كوناكري الغيني، والمغرب الفاسي. وسيتجنب "النادي الأزرق" مأزقا كان قد واجهه الموسم الماضي، حين تعارضت مواعيد جولاته الافتتاحية في البطولة الأفريقية مع مباريات المنتخب السوداني، في تصفيات ونهائيات كأس العرب "الدوحة 2026"، ما أرهق نجومه بسبب كثرة التنقلات. ويحظى الفريق السوداني هذه المرة بفرصة مثالية لتحقيق نتائج إيجابية؛ والتأهل للدور المقبل من دوري أبطال أفريقيا، نظرا لملاءمة جدول افتتاح مشواره مع مواعيد مباريات "صقور الجديان" أمام "أسود التيرانغا". مواجهات تاريخية بانتظار الهلال تنتظر الهلال مواجهات مرتقبة في دوري أبطال أفريقيا ؛ حيث يواجه أسفرت قرعة البطولات الأفريقية عن مواجهات صعبة للأندية المصرية في دور المجموعات. حيث وقع الزمالك في مجموعة تضم الأفريقي التونسي، مولودية الجزائر، ويانج أفريكانز التنزاني، مما يتطلب استعدادًا قويًا لضمان التأهل. تبدأ مباريات الزمالك بمواجهة الأفريقي في نهاية نوفمبر، تليها مباراة مع مولودية الجزائر في ديسمبر، ثم يانج أفريكانز في يناير. 

أما بيراميدز، فقد أوقعته القرعة في مجموعة تضم الهلال السوداني، حوريا الغيني، والمغرب الفاسي، حيث سيبدأ مشواره بمواجهة المغرب الفاسي. 

في الكونفدرالية، يواجه الأهلي الرجاء المغربي، بالإضافة إلى أول أغسطس الأنجولي وأسكو دي كارا التوجولي. تبدأ مباريات الأهلي بمواجهة أول أغسطس في القاهرة، تليها مباراة مع أسكو دي كارا في توجو، ثم الرجاء في ديسمبر. هذه القرعة تعكس تحديات كبيرة للأندية المصرية في السعي نحو تحقيق النجاح في البطولات الأفريقية.
